vulnerabilities.title: [CRITICAL] Buffer Overflow in BACnet Packet Parsing - NPDU Extraction
[HIGH] Array Index Out of Bounds in extractDeviceInstance and Related Methods
[HIGH] Integer Overflow in NPDU Length Calculation
[MEDIUM] Missing Input Validation in encodeValue Method
vulnerabilities.description:
## Vulnerability

The `encodeValue()` method (lines 559-581) lacks input validation for string lengths and numeric ranges. Particularly concerning:

1. Line 569 writes string length as a single byte without checking if the string exceeds 255 characters
2. Character-to-byte casting loses Unicode information
3. No buffer space validation before writing
4. No validation for NaN or Infinity numeric values

```java
if (value instanceof String) {
    String str = (String) value;
    buffer.put((byte) 0x75); // Character string
    buffer.put((byte) 0); // Encoding: ANSI X3.4
    buffer.put((byte) str.length());  // BUG: Truncates if length > 255
    for (char c : str.toCharArray()) {
        buffer.put((byte) c);  // BUG: Can overflow buffer, loses Unicode
    }
}
```

## OWASP Classification

**Category**: A04:2021 - Insecure Design  
**Reference**: https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design/  
**Description**: Lack of input validation in data encoding can lead to buffer overflows, data corruption, and protocol violations. The design fails to account for edge cases and maximum values defined by the protocol specification.

## Location

- **File**: `src/main/java/com/bacnet/emulator/service/BacnetService.java`
- **Lines**: 559-581
- **Method**: `encodeValue()`

## Risk Assessment

For the BACnet emulator:
1. Strings longer than 255 characters will be silently truncated in the length field but fully written, causing buffer overflow
2. Responses to legitimate BACnet clients may be malformed
3. Unicode characters are incorrectly encoded (cast to byte loses high bits)
4. Could cause integration test failures
5. May corrupt communication with real BACnet devices
6. ByteBuffer overflow causes thread crashes

## Suggested Fix

Add proper validation and error handling. See full code example in the detailed analysis document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add length validation for strings (max 255 chars)
- [ ] Use proper charset encoding (UTF-8) instead of casting to byte
- [ ] Handle case where UTF-8 encoding exceeds 255 bytes
- [ ] Add buffer space checks before all write operations
- [ ] Validate numeric values (reject NaN, Infinity)
- [ ] Add unit tests for edge cases (255 char string, 256 char string, Unicode, NaN, etc.)
- [ ] Add tests for buffer overflow scenarios
- [ ] Add integration test with various object value types

vulnerabilities.title: [MEDIUM] Race Condition in Device and Object Cache Refresh
vulnerabilities.description:
## Vulnerability

The `refreshDeviceCache()` method (lines 667-692) clears the entire cache and rebuilds it while concurrent packet handler threads access the same cache. This creates a race condition where legitimate BACnet requests can fail with 'device not found' errors during cache refresh.

```java
private void refreshDeviceCache() {
    while (running) {
        try {
            Thread.sleep(5000);
            
            deviceCache.clear();  // RACE: Other threads reading cache!
            objectCache.clear();  // RACE: Other threads reading cache!
            
            List<BacnetDevice> devices = deviceRepository.findByEnabledTrue();
            for (BacnetDevice device : devices) {
                deviceCache.put(device.getDeviceInstanceId(), device);
                // ... more population
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The window between `clear()` and `put()` operations leaves the cache empty, causing packet handlers to incorrectly report devices as not found.

## OWASP Classification

**Category**: A04:2021 - Insecure Design  
**Reference**: https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design/  
**Description**: The concurrent cache update design creates race conditions where the system state is inconsistent. This is a fundamental design flaw in how the cache is maintained under concurrent access, violating thread safety principles.

## Location

- **File**: `src/main/java/com/bacnet/emulator/service/BacnetService.java`
- **Lines**: 667-692
- **Method**: `refreshDeviceCache()`
- **Also affects**: Lines 259, 307, 318 (cache reads in packet handlers)

## Risk Assessment

For the BACnet emulator during integration testing:
1. Tests may intermittently fail when device lookups occur during cache refresh
2. Legitimate BACnet clients receive 'device not found' errors sporadically
3. Makes the emulator unreliable for its primary testing purpose
4. Creates difficult-to-reproduce bugs in test environments
5. May mask real issues in the BACnet client being tested
6. Undermines confidence in test results

## Suggested Fix

Use atomic cache swap to eliminate the race window. See full code example in the detailed analysis document using volatile CacheSnapshot pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `CacheSnapshot` class with immutable references
- [ ] Change cache fields to use volatile snapshot pattern
- [ ] Update all cache access points (approximately 10 locations)
- [ ] Remove direct `deviceCache.clear()` and `objectCache.clear()` calls
- [ ] Add concurrent stress test sending 100 requests/sec during cache refresh
- [ ] Verify zero 'device not found' errors during cache refresh
- [ ] Add unit test verifying atomic cache swap
- [ ] Add metrics/logging for cache refresh operations
- [ ] Document thread safety guarantees in javadoc

vulnerabilities.title: [MEDIUM] ByteBuffer Overflow in Encoding Methods
vulnerabilities.description:
## Vulnerability

Several encoding methods allocate fixed-size ByteBuffers (64, 256 bytes) without checking if the encoded data will fit. If the data exceeds buffer capacity, a `BufferOverflowException` is thrown, crashing the packet handler thread and preventing responses to clients.

Affected methods:
- `sendIAm()` - 256 byte buffer (line 401)
- `sendReadPropertyResponse()` - 256 byte buffer (line 444)
- `sendSimpleAck()` - 64 byte buffer (line 485)
- `sendErrorResponse()` - 64 byte buffer (line 511)

```java
private void sendReadPropertyResponse(...) {
    ByteBuffer buffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(256);  // Fixed size!
    // ... encoding that could exceed 256 bytes for long strings
    buffer.put((byte) 0x75);
    buffer.put((byte) str.length());
    for (char c : str.toCharArray()) {
        buffer.put((byte) c);  // BufferOverflowException if > 250 chars
    }
}
```

## OWASP Classification

**Category**: A04:2021 - Insecure Design  
**Reference**: https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design/  
**Description**: Fixed buffer allocation without validation of required space is a design flaw. The system should either dynamically allocate based on data size or validate data fits within buffer limits before encoding.

## Location

- **File**: `src/main/java/com/bacnet/emulator/service/BacnetService.java`
- **Lines**: 401 (`sendIAm`), 444 (`sendReadPropertyResponse`), 485 (`sendSimpleAck`), 511 (`sendErrorResponse`)
- **Methods**: Multiple encoding/response methods

## Risk Assessment

For the BACnet emulator tool:
1. Long device names or object descriptions cause buffer overflow
2. Packet handler threads crash when encoding oversized responses
3. Legitimate client requests lost without response
4. Reduces reliability and trustworthiness of the testing tool
5. Makes debugging client issues harder
6. Could be intentionally triggered by creating devices/objects with very long names

## Suggested Fix

Use dynamic buffer sizing with protocol limit or add proper validation. See full code examples in the detailed analysis document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace all fixed-size buffers with appropriately sized buffers (max 1476 bytes)
- [ ] Add try-catch for `BufferOverflowException` in all encoding methods
- [ ] Validate string lengths before encoding (truncate if needed)
- [ ] Add buffer space validation before each write operation
- [ ] Add unit tests with 200+ character names and descriptions
- [ ] Add logging when truncation occurs
- [ ] Add integration test creating devices/objects with maximum length fields
- [ ] Document field length limits in API documentation
- [ ] Consider adding validation in `DeviceService` and `ObjectService`
